title: Escalation Handoff to SRE + Incident Process (Support v2)
author: Owen Phillips
body:
## Purpose
This page defines **how Support hands off issues to SRE/oncall**, including:
- When an issue is a **Support escalation** vs a formal **incident**
- What information is required before paging/engaging SRE
- How to use **#incidents** (and incident-bot) to standardize the handoff
- How Support keeps the **customer loop** updated during investigation/mitigation

This is part of **Escalation Playbook v2** and is designed to improve time-to-mitigation while protecting paging hygiene.

---

## Definitions (use consistent language)
- **Support escalation:** A time-sensitive issue requiring engineering/SRE engagement but may not yet meet incident criteria (e.g., single-customer Dedicated capacity degradation, repeatable 5xx affecting one model in one region).
- **Incident:** A customer-impacting service event managed under the incident process (commander role, timeline, comms cadence, mitigation focus, follow-ups). Incidents usually involve broader impact, elevated error rate, or critical security/availability risk.
- **Customer thread:** The primary communication channel with the customer (Zendesk/Jira customer ticket/email/Slack Connect). Support owns customer-facing updates unless explicitly handed off.

---

## Decision: Escalation vs Incident
Use the table below to decide the right path. If uncertain, **start as an escalation and ask SRE whether to convert to an incident**.

### Quick decision table
| Scenario | Default action | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Elevated **5xx/timeouts** across a region/model for multiple customers | **Declare incident** | Use monitoring data when possible; do not wait for “more tickets” if dashboards confirm. |
| **Streaming disconnects** appear elevated (multiple customers, multiple orgs) | **Escalate to SRE; likely incident if elevated error rate** | If impact is broad and ongoing, declare incident to enforce comms cadence + coordination. |
| Single-customer issue likely caused by client/network (no correlated metrics) | **Support-led escalation (no incident)** | Avoid paging unless severity/contract requires. Gather evidence first. |
| Dedicated customer experiences capacity shortfall/latency spike during peak | **Escalate to SRE / Dedicated oncall** | Incident only if platform-level or multiple tenants impacted; otherwise handle as Dedicated escalation with customer comms + mitigation plan. |
| Private/VPC SSO/SAML outage blocking admin access | **Escalate to Private Deployments + Security; incident if widespread or security risk** | Treat customer details as restricted. |
| Suspected **security incident** (credential leak, unauthorized access, audit log anomaly) | **Engage Security immediately; follow security incident process** | Do not post details broadly; follow “restricted” handling. |

### Incident triggers (practical guidance)
Declare an incident when **any** of the following are true:
1) **Broad impact:** multiple customers/orgs impacted, or “likely broad impact” confirmed via metrics.
2) **SLO breach risk:** sustained error/latency suggests SLO breach for Hosted/Dedicated tiers.
3) **Critical functionality down:** auth outage, control plane outage, or core inference unavailable for a region.
4) **Sev0/Sev1:** per severity matrix (e.g., production down for enterprise tier, data integrity risk).
5) **Security risk:** suspected compromise, unauthorized access, or high-confidence security regression.

If you are seeing **customer-reported impact + correlated platform signals**, err toward declaring an incident.

---

## Before you page SRE: minimum triage checklist (10–15 minutes)
Paging with incomplete context slows down mitigation. Support should collect the following **before** engaging SRE (unless the situation is clearly P0/Sev0 and time-critical).

### Minimum required data (copy/paste into the escalation form)
**Customer + scope**
- Customer name + tier (Self-serve / Dedicated / Private / Enterprise)
- Deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Environment + region(s) (e.g., us-east, eu-west)
- Time window (start time, ongoing?, timezone)

**Impact**
- What broke? (5xx, timeouts, streaming disconnects, 429s, auth)
- Impact level: % of requests affected (if known), user-visible symptoms
- Business impact statement (customer-provided OK): “prod down,” “partial outage,” “degraded latency,” etc.

**Repro / evidence**
- Request IDs (at least 3) and timestamps
- Model name + version/pin (if applicable)
- Endpoint + route (chat/completions/embeddings/etc.)
- Error codes + representative error bodies (redact secrets)
- SDK + version / HTTP client + version

**What we tried**
- Any mitigations attempted (retries, increased timeouts, region failover, model rollback/pin change)
- Any configuration changes shortly before the issue (customer or Redwood side)

**Customer comms**
- Link to the customer thread/ticket
- Current customer expectation (next update time, any SLA language already referenced)

### Redaction and handling rules
- Do **not** paste customer secrets, tokens, private keys, or raw prompts containing sensitive data.
- If the incident involves a **Private/enterprise account with restricted data**, use:
  - Restricted Jira fields/attachments where available
  - Slack: summarize at high level; share sensitive artifacts only in approved restricted channels

---

## How to engage SRE/oncall (standard workflow)
Support should use this sequence to ensure consistent routing and record-keeping.

### Step 1 — Create/confirm a Support escalation ticket
1) Ensure there is an existing Support ticket (customer-facing or internal escalation ticket).
2) Confirm required fields are filled in (see: “Jira Ticket Template and Required Fields”).
3) Assign severity per matrix (P0–P4 / Sev0–Sev3). If uncertain, state “proposed severity” and why.

### Step 2 — Start an incident thread in #incidents (even for many escalations)
**Where:** Slack channel **#incidents**

**Why:** #incidents provides a single searchable timeline and makes converting to a formal incident fast.

**How:** Use incident-bot’s “Support Escalation” workflow (preferred) or follow the manual template below.

#### Incident-bot (preferred)
- Run the **Support Escalation** workflow
- Fill out the prompts using the minimum required data above
- Include Jira key(s) and any dashboards if available

#### Manual message template (if bot unavailable)
Post a new message in #incidents with:
- **Title:** [ESCALATION] <symptom> – <region> – <customer/tier> – <start time>
- **Severity (proposed):** P? / Sev?
- **Summary:** 2–3 sentences
- **Impact:** who/what is affected
- **Signals:** request IDs + timestamps; error codes
- **Suspected component:** gateway / scheduler / runtime / auth / private installer
- **Links:** ticket link, dashboards, relevant runbooks
- **Customer comms:** next update time and who owns it

### Step 3 — Page SRE/oncall only when criteria are met
Paging should be used for:
- Clear P0/Sev0–Sev1 events
- Confirmed platform-level degradation
- Contractual after-hours coverage requirements (tier-specific)
- Time-sensitive mitigations requiring engineering access (e.g., routing/failover)

If unsure whether to page, ask in #incidents and tag **@Rafael Mendes** (or current SRE oncall) with “page needed?” plus your evidence.

### Step 4 — SRE decision: keep as escalation vs declare incident
SRE/oncall will decide whether to:
- Keep it as a **Support escalation** (tracked in #incidents thread + ticket)
- Convert to a formal **incident** (assign IC, start incident roles, comms cadence)

Support should not wait for a perfect diagnosis to support the incident decision. Provide impact + evidence; SRE will coordinate deeper triage.

---

## During an incident: Support responsibilities
When an incident is declared, Support remains responsible for customer communication unless otherwise agreed.

### Support responsibilities checklist
- Keep the customer thread updated per tier SLA (first response + update cadence)
- Ensure customer asks are captured and relayed to incident thread (without sensitive data)
- Collect additional request IDs/log context as requested by SRE
- Confirm whether the customer can apply any **safe mitigations** (known workarounds)

### Update cadence (minimum expectations)
Follow the SLA-by-tier table. If you don’t have the table handy, use these defaults until corrected:
- **Enterprise/Dedicated/Private:** updates every **30–60 minutes** during active mitigation, then every **2–4 hours** while monitoring.
- **Self-serve:** updates every **2–4 hours** for significant degradations; faster if user-facing outage.

If SRE provides a comms cadence in #incidents, mirror it.

---

## Customer comms: what to say (and what not to say)
### Principles
- Be specific about **what we know**, **what we’re doing**, and **when we’ll update next**.
- Avoid speculation and root-cause guesses.
- Don’t promise exact ETAs unless SRE confirms.
- Offer **safe-to-share mitigations** only if validated for the customer’s deployment mode and version.

### Recommended structure for updates
1) Acknowledge impact and that investigation is active
2) Current status (investigating / mitigation in progress / monitoring)
3) Any customer actions (if applicable) + why they help
4) Next update time (explicit)

### Examples (short)
**Investigation started**
“Thanks for the details — we’re actively investigating elevated <symptom> impacting <scope>. We’ve engaged our oncall reliability team and are reviewing request IDs from <time window>. Next update by <time>.”

**Mitigation applied**
“We’ve applied a mitigation to reduce <symptom> in <region>. Early signals show improvement, and we’re continuing to monitor. Next update by <time>.”

**Monitoring**
“Service metrics have returned to normal levels as of <time>. We’re monitoring closely for recurrence and will follow up with a summary once we confirm stability.”

(For full templates, use the Customer Comms Templates page.)

---

## Workarounds: when to recommend them
Only recommend workarounds that are:
- Documented in **Known Issues & Workarounds** and marked **safe-to-share**, OR
- Explicitly validated by SRE/engineering in the current escalation thread

Common safe mitigations (validate applicability first):
- SDK retry/backoff for transient 429/timeouts
- Adjust client timeouts for long generations
- Streaming reconnect pattern (resume/retry with idempotency as applicable)
- Model pin rollback to a previously stable version (Hosted)
- Region failover guidance (Hosted/Dedicated if configured)

If a workaround risks data loss or changes output behavior materially, call that out explicitly and ask the customer to confirm.

---

## Required artifacts: what must exist by the end of the event
Whether escalation or incident, ensure the following are recorded:
- Link to the primary customer ticket/thread
- #incidents thread link
- Request IDs + timestamps (and any relevant logs/headers, redacted)
- Mitigation applied (what, when, by whom)
- Customer-facing summary of resolution

For formal incidents, SRE will own the incident record and follow-up items; Support should ensure customer questions are represented in follow-ups (e.g., “prevent recurrence,” “SLA credits process,” “RCA timeline”).

---

## Escalation-to-incident conversion (common pitfall)
If an escalation becomes broader than initially believed:
1) Post in the #incidents thread: “Recommend converting to incident — new evidence: <metrics/tickets>.”
2) Ensure customer comms are aligned: if we declare an incident, the customer should receive an update within the next promised window.
3) If a status page update is required, follow the Support Escalation Comms Alignment doc.

---

## Appendix A — What “good” looks like (handoff example)
**Message in #incidents:**
- [ESCALATION] Streaming disconnects – us-east – Enterprise (Dedicated) – started 09:40 PT
- Proposed severity: P1 / Sev1
- Impact: customer reports ~15–25% of streaming sessions terminating early; started after traffic increase; ongoing
- Evidence: request IDs: abc123 (09:43:12), def456 (09:44:01), ghi789 (09:46:18)
- Model/route: chat.completions stream=true, model=redwood-verified-llama-70b (pinned)
- Customer env: Dedicated pool; region us-east
- Links: SUP-4921, dashboard <link>, runbook <link>
- Customer comms: Support owner @<name>; next update promised 10:30 PT

This contains enough context for SRE to begin triage immediately.

---

## Appendix B — Routing notes (high level)
- **Auth/SSO/SAML (Private):** Private Deployments + Security
- **429s/rate limit behavior:** API gateway/rate-limit SME + SRE if global degradation suspected
- **5xx/timeouts:** SRE first if broad; otherwise component owner after initial signals
- **Dedicated capacity/latency:** Dedicated oncall / SRE (depending on symptom scope)

See the Escalation Paths & Ownership Map for the authoritative routing list.
